validity.recommendation: no action on existence/classification/duplicate -- real, FERC-certificated, never-built project; see separate spec concern on Diameter and attribution concern on Owner1
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently documented FERC-certificated project, not a GEM-only entity. Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline, L.P. (Creole Trail/CCTPL) and its affiliate Sabine Pass Liquefaction Expansion, LLC jointly filed on September 30, 2013 (FERC Docket Nos. CP13-552-000 and CP13-553-000); FERC issued a Federal Register notice of the application on 2014-12-23 (2014-29956) describing 'about 104.3 miles of 42- and 36-inch-diameter pipeline' adding 1.5 Bcf/d, and FERC granted the certificate on 2015-04-06 in 151 FERC P 61,012 (Zone 1 loops + Zone 2 extension/laterals, $610.5M). A separate FERC order, 148 FERC P 61,200 (2014-09-18, denying Sierra Club rehearing in the related LNG-terminal docket CP14-12-001), independently restates the same Sept 30, 2013 filing date and names 'Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline, L.P.' as the CP13-553-000 applicant. EIA's own 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook (dated 2026-08 release, Historical Projects (1996-2024) tab) carries this exact project as two rows keyed to Docket CP13-553 ('Creole Trail Expansion Project 2', 104.3 mi, $610M, 1500 MMcf/d, 42in): Excel row 839 (Approved, Last Updated 2016-08-25) and Excel row 1130 (Cancelled, Last Updated 2020-06-11) -- both still present side by side in the newest release, documenting the full Approved->Cancelled history in one dated file. Not GEM-only -- three independent origins (FERC twice, over separate dockets; EIA). CLASSIFICATION: correctly classified as a gas transmission pipeline expansion (interstate, FERC NGA section 7(c) certificated, Part 284 rate zones) -- not a gathering/feeder line. DUPLICATE: checked against the full 44-row roster. P7797 'Creole Trail Pipeline' (proposed 2025, cap 930 MMcf/d, Gillis Compressor Station + new Tarpon Compressor Station work) is a legitimately DIFFERENT, later, smaller compression-only project on the same CCTPL system -- not a duplicate of P2522 (the 2013-2015-vintage 104.3mi/1500MMcf/d Zone 1/Zone 2 pipe-and-compression Reversal/Expansion Project, cancelled circa 2020). Also distinct from EIA's OWN separate 'Creole Trail Expansion Project 1' (Docket CP12-351, 0.04 mi, $100M, completed 2015-04-27) -- a smaller, already-built, earlier project not tracked as a separate GEM PID as far as this sweep could determine. See cross_row_leads note on P7797 in researcher_notes below (no verifiable URL found for it this pass -- see status_reviews entry).

validity.recommendation: add 36 to the recorded Diameter (currently 42.00 only) -- project used mixed 42-inch and 36-inch pipe
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Diameter=42.00in only. Two independent FERC-family documents state the project was built with MIXED diameters: the Federal Register notice of application (2014-12-23, 2014-29956) states the project 'would add about 104.3 miles of 42- and 36-inch-diameter pipeline'; the FERC certificate order (151 FERC P 61,012, para. 13-14, 21) details 13.9mi and 24.5mi Zone 1 loops at 42in, a 48.5mi Zone 2 extension at 42in, and FOUR Zone 2 laterals of which 'three, 36-inch-diameter laterals and one 42-inch-diameter lateral.' This is a material, corroborated discrepancy -- not merely a rounding difference. Note EIA's own workbook (Historical Projects tab, Docket CP13-553 row) also records only '42' for Pipeline Diameter (Inches), so EIA's own dataset is at least as incomplete as GEM's here -- this is a genuine documentation gap in both trackers relative to the underlying FERC order, not a GEM-specific error to overcorrect on the strength of EIA alone. Recommend Diameter = '42, 36' per GEM's multi-value diameter convention, sourced to the FERC certificate order + Federal Register notice (both name Creole Trail and this project explicitly).

validity.recommendation: change Owner1 from 'Cheniere Energy' to 'Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline, L.P.'s direct parent, Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P.' -- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (the recorded owner) does not directly own the pipeline
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Owner1='Cheniere Energy' at 100%, uncited. The actual direct 100% owner of Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline, L.P. (CCTPL, the project entity) is Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P. (NYSE American: CQP), a separately publicly-traded MLP -- NOT Cheniere Energy, Inc. (NYSE American: LNG), the ultimate parent, which per its own investor-relations page owns only '100% of the general partner interest and a 48.6% limited partner interest in Cheniere Partners' (as of 2022, structure unchanged as of this sweep per the same live page). Two genuinely separate origins corroborate CCTPL sitting under Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P. rather than Cheniere Energy, Inc. directly: (1) Cheniere's own investor-relations 'company-information' page (lngir.cheniere.com) states 'Cheniere Partners also owns the Creole Trail Pipeline...'; (2) Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P.'s OWN separately SEC-registered 10-K (CIK 0001383650, FY2025 filing, Exhibit 21.1 Subsidiaries of the Registrant) lists 'Cheniere Creole Trail Pipeline, L.P.' as a direct Delaware subsidiary. A distinct SEC filer's own exhibit is a genuinely independent origin from the parent's marketing/IR pages, per this project's independence rule. Recommend Operator (see fills[]) and Owner1 both be corrected to reflect Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P. as the direct 100% owner, distinct from the ultimate parent Cheniere Energy, Inc.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Sheet's recorded Status='cancelled' is RIGHT, but currently reads ShelvedCancelledType='inferred'. Sourced evidence upgrades this to 'confirmed': EIA's own Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, 2021-01 dated release (Historical Projects (1996-2020) tab, Excel row 195) carries this exact project (Docket CP13-553, 'Creole Trail Expansion Project 2') as 'Cancelled', Last Updated 2020-06-11 -- this is the first EIA release to carry the Cancelled row (the prior scraped release, 2020-03, still shows only 'Approved'/'Approved/On Hold', at Excel row 144 of its own Historical Projects (1996-2019) tab) -- a dated, discrete status-change record, not a dormancy inference on GEM's part. Corroborating by omission: Cheniere's CURRENT corporate page (fetched live 2026-09-10) describes only the original 94-mile mainline (in service spring 2008) with zero mention of the Zone 1/Zone 2 Reversal/Expansion Project, consistent with it never being built and staying cancelled six years after EIA's flip. No FERC order formally vacating/withdrawing the CP13-553-000 certificate was found (searched elibrary.ferc.gov docket listing and Federal Register notices after 2015); FERC's certificate order itself (para 16) notes no shipper had executed a binding precedent agreement for the Zone 2 capacity as of the 2015 order, a plausible mechanism for the project quietly lapsing without a formal withdrawal order. Given the EIA record is a single, dated, independent, government-source status-change event (not GEM-derived) plus the corroborating-by-omission evidence from Cheniere's own current materials, this rises to a sourced 'confirmed' cancellation with CancelledYear=2020, tier medium (one direct dated source + one corroborating-by-omission source, not two fully independent direct confirmations of the cancellation act itself). Searched for but did not find: a Cheniere press release or 8-K explicitly announcing withdrawal of the Zone 2 expansion; a FERC order granting withdrawal/vacating CP13-553-000.
